title: ZIA API rate limits and how the Python SDK retries

prose.text: ZIA enforces per-endpoint limits and answers 429 when they are exceeded; the Python SDK retries a small set of statuses on its own. The Go SDK's retry behavior is in [[shared.sdk-go.retries]], and the SCIM limit is in [[zia.scim.operations]].

prose.label: SDK retries.
prose.text: {{sdk-max-retries-default}} Which statuses the executor retries is in [[zia.sdk-python.request-conventions:retry-statuses-docstring-mismatch]]. The SDK's two lists of retryable statuses disagree {{divergence:retryable-status-sets}}. {{sdk-wait-from-headers}} {{sdk-max-retry-seconds}}

checks.do: Which weight class the failing call falls in (delete, write, read) against the per-second, per-minute and per-hour ceilings.
Whether the client retried: the status was one the SDK retries, and the retry budget was not exhausted or capped by maxRetrySeconds.
Whether a 409 on a write was the edit lock held by another admin session, which the SDK retries on its own schedule.

zia-two-bounds.statement: Every ZIA endpoint has two rate limits: a lower-bound limit against short bursts and an upper-bound limit against sustained volume.

quotes: Every ZIA endpoint has two different types of rate limit:
A lower bound limit (protects against high bursts over a short period)
An upper bound limit (protects against high volume over a long period)

zia-default-weights.statement: Endpoints are weighted: Heavy, typically DELETE, defaults to 1 request per minute and 4 per hour; Medium, POST and PUT, to 1 per second and 400 per hour; Light, GET, to 2 per second and 1,000 per hour.

evidence.after: Every endpoint is assigned a weight with a default rate limit:

zia-429-headers.statement: An exceeded limit returns HTTP 429, and ZIA responses carry x-ratelimit-limit, x-ratelimit-remaining and x-ratelimit-reset, the last being the seconds left in the current window.

quotes: When the rate limit is exceeded, an HTTP 429 response code is returned.
`x-ratelimit-reset`: Time (in seconds) remaining in the current window after which rate limit resets

sdk-max-retries-default.statement: The Python request executor retries up to the rateLimit maxRetries setting, which defaults to 2.

sdk-wait-from-headers.statement: The retry wait comes from Retry-After plus one second, or else from the rate-limit reset header plus one second; with neither header the request is not retried and an error is returned.

sdk-max-retry-seconds.statement: A rateLimit maxRetrySeconds setting caps the wait: a computed backoff above it raises RetryTooLong instead of sleeping.

zia-edit-lock-retry.statement: For ZIA a 409 whose body contains EDIT_LOCK_NOT_AVAILABLE, meaning another admin session holds the edit lock, is retried with a backoff of 5 seconds doubling per attempt and capped at 60.

retryable-status-sets.summary: The SDK holds two different sets of retryable statuses: a constant and a helper that include 500 and 502, and the executor's own check that does not.

positions.says: RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES is {429, 500, 502, 503, 504}, and the utils helper tests membership in it.
The executor's is_retryable_status returns true only for 429, 503 and 504, though its docstring lists 500 and 502 too.

retryable-status-sets.impact: A 500 or 502 from ZIA is not retried by the request executor's rate-limit path even though the constant suggests it would be.
